name: Nude / white waterline eyeliner

card.summary: Pale pencil on the lower waterline, said to brighten the eyes; popular tip, no studies behind it.
card.note: Products contact the eye surface; no cosmetic studies found.

quick.overview:
Nude or white waterline eyeliner is a makeup technique where a light pencil is applied to the inner rim of the lower lid. Users say it makes eyes look brighter and more awake.

No published study has tested the cosmetic effect, so the claims rest on user reports.
quick.mechanism: The light color is said to contrast with the dark rim and reduce the look of shadow or redness at the lid margin, making the eye appear larger.
quick.risks: Anything applied to the waterline touches the eye surface; waterproof, eye-safe products are generally preferred per general makeup references. No studies of waterline-specific harms were found.

lead: Nude or white waterline eyeliner is a makeup technique in which a skin-toned, beige or white pencil is applied to the lower waterline, the thin inner rim of the lower eyelid. People use it to make their eyes look brighter, more awake and larger, and to soften the look of redness or shadow along the lid margin [3][4].

It belongs to the long history of eyeliner, which dates to ancient Egypt and Mesopotamia [1]. Makeup artists quoted in fashion and beauty media describe the light shade as making the whites of the eyes look larger against the lashes, giving a more open, rested look than dark liner on the same spot [3][4]. Nude shades are presented as a softer, less obvious option than opaque white, which reads as a more dramatic brightening [4].
The advice comes from makeup artists, brands and users. No published clinical study has measured its effect on perceived eye size or attractiveness.

chain: Pale pencil on the lower waterline
Reduces visible redness and contrast at the lid margin
Eyes look brighter, more open and more awake
angle.text: A light liner on the lower waterline is used to make eyes appear larger and less tired within a few seconds of application. It sits alongside other eye-opening makeup such as tightlining the upper lash line and curling lashes.

infobox: Light-colored (nude, beige or white) eye pencil or gel liner

paras: The technique places a pale pencil along the lower waterline, in contrast to the dark liner traditionally used for definition. Wikipedia describes the related practice of tight lining, in which liner sits against the lash roots or waterline and makes lashes seem to begin farther back on the lid; it notes that waterproof products are generally preferred because of the eye's sensitive surface [1].

L'Oreal Paris's beauty magazine lists the lower waterline as the main placement for nude liner, with other uses including a dab at the inner corners for a wider-eyed look, a shade lighter than skin on the center of the lid to add dimension, and a nude wing under darker shadow in place of a classic flick. It also advises avoiding heavy liner on the lower lash line to keep the eyes looking open [4].

Brand and magazine sources describe the effects as making eyes look bigger and more open, neutralizing redness at the waterline, and giving tired eyes a more awake look [4]. Makeup artist Kasey Spickard, quoted in W Magazine, describes the contrast between the lash base and the whites of the eyes as making them look brighter and slightly larger [3].

Artists quoted in the same coverage describe related tightlining as making lashes look fuller and, depending on placement, subtly elongating or lifting eye shapes [3]. For smaller eyes, one suggestion is to line only the outer two-thirds of the upper waterline and optionally use a nude pencil on the lower waterline [3].

The tip circulates mainly in mainstream makeup coverage and tutorials, and is part of the broader set of techniques used to enhance eye area appearance, including eyebrow shaping and lash enhancement. The sources reviewed contain little discussion of it on dedicated looksmaxxing forums.

Products on the waterline sit against the eye surface. Beauty sources emphasize practical points such as waterproof or waterline-specific formulas to limit smudging and wiping the waterline dry first if eyes water [3]. The beauty articles reviewed do not give figures on irritation or infection from waterline liner.

No studies found on the cosmetic effect of light waterline liner. A pediatric dermatology report described using a white eyeliner pencil to mark capillary malformations before laser treatment, a medical use unrelated to cosmetic eye brightening [2].
